symptom: Shadow Evidence scope.runKind/modelVersion used generic \S boundary regexes. Draft 2020-12 schema-only consumers could disagree with the ECMAScript trim-canonical runtime on U+FEFF and U+0085; terminal-newline anchoring was also weaker than exact string admission. Synthetic Python/JavaScript probes confirmed the lexical mismatch. No private data, production incident or external source authority was observed.
lesson: A scope identity requiring exact trim-canonical strings needs both nonblank admission and rejection of leading/trailing ECMAScript trim code points. Generic \S is not portable across Python and JavaScript, and a $ anchor may admit terminal newline in some engines.
guardrail: For scope.runKind and scope.modelVersion, use the explicit ECMAScript whitespace complement at both edges, permit internal Unicode/line breaks, and require true end-of-string via negative lookahead. Retain runtime digest, semantic checks and path/privacy scans. This is schema-only lexical parity, not source authenticity, evaluation readiness or production authority.
